scope: Resolve the 5 NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY findings (BCS-Y-0004, 0007, 0008, 0009, 0010) - all lobby-crypto and lobby-channel entries in the catalog. For each, identify what the catalog intended to point at, propose the correct VA, and characterize the bug pattern.

method.step1: Re-read each entry from manifests/symbols.json to get name, current address, notes
method.step2: Compare sourceRefs for matching class/function name and any embedded address
method.step3: Try the +0x400000 shift the catalog validation report pass already ruled out, plus +0x800000 (image_base + relabeling delta)
method.step4: Pull the LobbyCryptEngine vftable from Ghidra at the stated vtable VA to read the actual 9 function-pointer slots stored in the binary
method.step5: Decompile candidate VAs to verify slot semantics match the catalog notes (dtor, PrepareHandshake, SetSessionKey, Encrypt/Decrypt with 32-byte AND-mask quirk, BuildHeader)
method.step6: Propose the corrected VA per entry; flag any false-positive PASSes uncovered in the process

root_cause.summary: The catalog stores 0x005Axxxx for every entry in this batch where the real VA in ffxivgame.exe is 0x00DAxxxx (delta = +0x00800000). Earlier transcription appears to have stripped the high half-byte (0x00DA -> 0x005A) when copying function names like FUN_00da1e40 into the address field, possibly via a regex that captured the wrong nibble or by manual two-character truncation.
evidence: LobbyCryptEngine::vftable at 0x01127698 stores 9 dwords whose values are all 0x00DAxxxx and resolve to Ghidra symbols FUN_00daXXXX (slots 0,1,4,6,7 match the 5 broken catalog entries verbatim).
Decompilation of FUN_00da1590 shows the Test Ticket Data seed copy + __time64 + writes to param_1+0x8 and param_2+0x34/0x74 that the catalog notes for BCS-Y-0007 PrepareHandshake describe verbatim.
Decompilation of FUN_00da18d0 shows the 'EnctyptPackedPacket' log line and the AND 0xffe0 round-down-to-32 quirk for BCS-Y-0009 Encrypt.
Decompilation of FUN_00da0f30 shows the matching 32-byte round-down quirk for BCS-Y-0010 Decrypt, calling FUN_0045abb0 (BF_decrypt path).

Decompilation of FUN_00da2ad0 (46 bytes) shows the BasePacketHeader build sequence (byte 0 = (in & 0xFFFFFF14) | 0x14, byte 1 = 0, byte 2..3 = [this+0x1c], byte 8..11 = _time64), matching lobby_proto_channel.h slot-2 documentation for BCS-Y-0004 BuildHeader.

DumpSymbolsAtAddress confirms 0x009A1590, 0x009A1670, 0x009A18D0, 0x009A0F30, 0x009A1E40, 0x009A2AD0, 0x005A1590, 0x005A1670, 0x005A18D0, 0x005A0F30, 0x005A2AD0 all have (no symbols), so neither the catalog VA nor the +0x400000 shift lands on the real function. Only the +0x800000 shift (0x00DAxxxx) does.

false_positive_uncovered.actual_finding: The catalog validation report pass marked this PASS because Ghidra DOES have a function FUN_005a1e40 (21 bytes) at that VA, but it is an unrelated wrapper that calls (*vtable[0x40])(100) and an indirect dispatch via [result+0x1c]. It is NOT ~LobbyCryptEngine. The real ~LobbyCryptEngine is FUN_00da1e40 at 0x00DA1E40 (18 bytes, sets vftable then frees [this+0x30] via _free per the catalog notes). BCS-Y-0006 needs the same +0x00800000 fix.

entries.name: LobbyProtoChannel::ClientPacketBuilder::BuildHeader
entries.finding: NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY; insn= (no instruction at catalog VA at all)

name_evidence.decomp_confirms: FUN_00da2ad0 writes (byte0 & 0xFFFFFF14)|0x14, byte1=0, bytes 2..3 from [this+0x1c], bytes 8..11 from low 32 bits of _time64(NULL) - exact match for the catalog notes

entries.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A2AD0 to 0x00DA2AD0; classification should move from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000 in the validation report; entry is salvageable, no live capture work needed

entries.name: LobbyCryptEngine::PrepareHandshake
entries.finding: NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY; insn= (no instruction at catalog VA at all)
entries.shift_proposed_plus_0x800000: 0x00DA1590 -> Ghidra: FUN_00da1590 (170 bytes), at slot 1 of LobbyCryptEngine::vftable

name_evidence.decomp_confirms: FUN_00da1590 calls _strncpy(param_1+0x10, "Test Ticket Data", 0x20), __time64 -> param_1+0x8, _strncpy(param_2+0x34, param_1+0x10, 0x40), writes param_1+0x8 to param_2+0x74 - exact match for the catalog notes (Test Ticket Data seed copy to this+0x10, time low 32 bits to this+0x8 and req+0x74)

entries.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A1590 to 0x00DA1590; classification should move from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000; entry is salvageable

entries.name: LobbyCryptEngine::SetSessionKey
entries.shift_proposed_plus_0x800000: 0x00DA1670 -> Ghidra: FUN_00da1670 (125 bytes), at slot 4 of LobbyCryptEngine::vftable

name_evidence.decomp_confirms: FUN_00da1670 logs 'InitializeSecureSession(INIT)', then enters a long body that frees [this+0x30] via _free. The catalog notes (frees old BF_KEY, mallocs 4168 bytes, builds 16-byte key, calls BF_set_key) match the FUN_0045abf0 (BF_set_key) call path documented elsewhere; only the prologue is exposed by the decompiler's first-block summary but the entry point and free-old-key behavior align.
name_evidence.interior_note: catalog_validation_report.json reported the catalog VA was 'interior of FUN_005a1650' - that surrounding function is unrelated to crypto, not the real SetSessionKey at all

entries.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A1670 to 0x00DA1670; classification should move from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000; entry is salvageable

entries.name: LobbyCryptEngine::Encrypt
entries.finding: NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY; insn= (no instruction at catalog VA at all)
entries.shift_proposed_plus_0x800000: 0x00DA18D0 -> Ghidra: FUN_00da18d0 (74 bytes), at slot 6 of LobbyCryptEngine::vftable

name_evidence.decomp_confirms: FUN_00da18d0 logs 'EnctyptPackedPacket' (sic, the binary has this typo), checks [this+0x30] != 0, then calls FUN_0045ab60(buf, buf, len & 0xffe0). The AND 0xffe0 is exactly the round-down-to-32 quirk the catalog notes call out (= AND 0xFFFFFFE0). FUN_0045ab60 is the BF_encrypt-per-block helper.

entries.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A18D0 to 0x00DA18D0; classification should move from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000; entry is salvageable

entries.name: LobbyCryptEngine::Decrypt
entries.finding: NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY; insn=MOV EAX,dword ptr [EDX + 0x1c]; interior of FUN_005a0f20@0x005A0F20
entries.shift_proposed_plus_0x800000: 0x00DA0F30 -> Ghidra: FUN_00da0f30 (32 bytes), at slot 7 of LobbyCryptEngine::vftable

name_evidence.decomp_confirms: FUN_00da0f30 checks [this+0x30] != 0, then calls FUN_0045abb0(buf, buf, len & 0xffe0). Identical shape to Encrypt but with BF_decrypt helper FUN_0045abb0. The AND 0xffe0 confirms the 32-byte round-down quirk.
name_evidence.interior_note: catalog_validation_report.json reported the catalog VA was 'interior of FUN_005a0f20' - that surrounding function is unrelated, not the real Decrypt

entries.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A0F30 to 0x00DA0F30; classification should move from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000; entry is salvageable

summary.uniform_action: Update address field of BCS-Y-0004, 0007, 0008, 0009, 0010 by +0x00800000 (catalog 0x005Axxxx -> real VA 0x00DAxxxx); reclassify all 5 in the catalog_validation_report.json report from NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000. All function semantics in the catalog notes match the verified decompilations at the corrected VAs.

ancillary_findings.name: LobbyCryptEngine::~LobbyCryptEngine
ancillary_findings.finding: FALSE_POSITIVE_PASS: catalog address 0x005A1E40 happens to land on an unrelated 21-byte function (FUN_005a1e40) that calls (*vtable[0x40])(100) and an indirect dispatch via [result+0x1c]. This is NOT the destructor. The real ~LobbyCryptEngine is FUN_00da1e40 at 0x00DA1E40 (18 bytes, sets *param_1 = LobbyCryptEngine::vftable then _free(param_1[0xc])), confirmed by both the vtable slot 0 dump and decompilation. BCS-Y-0006 needs the same +0x00800000 correction as the other 5 entries.
ancillary_findings.recommended_action: FIX_VA: change address from 0x005A1E40 to 0x00DA1E40; downgrade the catalog validation report pass classification from PASS to TYPO_SHIFT_0x800000; out-of-scope for the not function entry investigation pass task (which only covers NOT_FUNCTION_ENTRY) but should be flagged for the next catalog cleanup pass

open_questions: Are there other entries in the catalog that share the +0x800000 typo pattern but PASSED the catalog validation report pass by coincidence (like BCS-Y-0006)? A targeted scan over all entries whose address starts with 0x005A or 0x009A could surface them. Symbols.json appears to use 0x009Axxxx for some lobby entries (BCS-Y-0019 through 0025) which the catalog validation report pass PASSED at face value - these would need re-verification against vtable / RTTI evidence rather than just function-existence to confirm they are not the same kind of false-positive.
